sanskrit: yan manyur jāyām āvahat saṃkalpasya gṛhād adhi | ka āsañ janyāḥ ke varāḥ ka u jyeṣṭhavaro 'bhavat ||
english: When Manyu brought forth the bride from the house of Saṃkalpa — who were the wedding-party, who were the suitors, and who became the chief suitor?

sanskrit: tapaś caivāstāṃ karma ca- -antar mahaty arṇave | ta āsan janyās te varāḥ sa u jyeṣṭhavaro 'bhavat ||
english: Tapas and Karman both dwelt within the great ocean — they were the wedding-party, they were the suitors, and Tapas was indeed the chief suitor.

sanskrit: daśa sākam ajāyanta devā devebhyaḥ paraḥ | yo vai tāṃ vidyān nāmathā sa vā adya mahad vadet ||
english: Ten gods were born together, transcending the gods. Whoever truly knows their names would speak a great thing today.

sanskrit: prāṇāpāṇau cakṣuḥ śrotram akṣitiś ca kṣitiś ca yā | vyānodāno vāṅ manas te vā ākūtim ā vahan ||
english: Prāṇa and Apāna, sight and hearing, the imperishable and what perishes, Vyāna, Udāna, speech and mind — these carried purpose within them.

sanskrit: ajātā āsann ṛtavo 'tho dhātā bṛhaspatiḥ | indrāgnī aśvinā tarhi kaṃ te jyeṣṭham upāsata ||
english: The seasons were yet unborn, and likewise Dhātṛ and Bṛhaspati, Indra, Agni, and the two Aśvins — whom did they then attend as eldest?

sanskrit: tapaś caivāstāṃ karma ca- -antar mahaty arṇave | tapo ha jajñe karmaṇas taṃ te jyeṣṭham upāsata ||
english: Tapas and Karman both dwelt within the great ocean; Tapas was born from Karman — him they attended as eldest.

sanskrit: kuta indraḥ kutaḥ somaḥ kuto agnir ajāyata | kutas tvaṣṭā sam abhavad dhātā sam abhavat kutaḥ ||
english: Whence was Indra born, whence Soma, whence did Agni come into being? Whence did Tvaṣṭṛ come together, whence did Dhātṛ come together?

sanskrit: indrād indraḥ somāt somo agner agnir ajāyata | tvaṣṭā ha jajñe tvaṣṭur dhātā dhātur ajāyata ||
english: From Indra came Indra, from Soma came Soma, from Agni Agni was born; Tvaṣṭṛ was indeed born from Tvaṣṭṛ, Dhātṛ arose from Dhātṛ.

sanskrit: ye ta āsan daśa jātā devā devebhyaḥ paraḥ | putrebhyo lokaṃ dattvā kasmin te loka āsate ||
english: Those ten who were born, gods transcending the gods — having granted the world to their sons, in what world do they now abide?

sanskrit: yeto bhūmiḥ purvāsīd yām addhātaya id viduḥ | ke tasyāṃ devā āsate kasminn u sādhiśritā ||
english: That which was the primordial earth, which Addhātayas alone have known — what gods dwell upon it, and in what does it rest, with all therein?

sanskrit: kutaḥ keśān kutaḥ snāva kuto asthīny ābharat | aṅgā parvāṇi majjānaṃ ko māṃsaṃ kuta ābharat ||
english: From where did he bring the hair, from where the sinews, from where did he bring the bones? Who brought the limbs and joints and marrow, from where did he bring the flesh?

sanskrit: yadā keśān asthi snāva māṃsaṃ majjānam ābharat | śarīraṃ kṛtvā pādavat kaṃ lokam anu prāviśat ||
english: When he brought together hair, bone, sinew, flesh, and marrow — having fashioned a body with feet, into what world did he then enter?

sanskrit: saṃsico nāma te devā ye saṃbhāraiḥ samabharan | sarvaṃ saṃsicya martyaṃ devāḥ puruṣam āviśan ||
english: Saṃsica — so are those gods named, who assembled him with their materials; having completely fashioned the mortal, the gods entered into the person.

sanskrit: śiro hastāv atho bāhū jihvāṃ grīvāś ca kīkasāḥ | pṛṣṭīr barjahye pārśve kas tat sam adadhād ṛṣiḥ ||
english: The head and hands, and the arms, the tongue and neck and vertebrae, the back-ribs, the spine, and the flanks — what ṛṣi fitted all that together?

sanskrit: ūrū pādāv aṣṭhīvantau śroṇī hastāv atho mukham | tvacā prāvṛtya tat sarvaṃ saṃdhā sam adadhān mahī ||
english: The thighs and feet, the knee-joints, the hips and hands, and the face — wrapping all that with skin, the great Saṃdhā joined it together.

sanskrit: yat tac charīram apayat saṃdhayā saṃhitaṃ mahat | yenedam adya rocate ko asmin varṇam ābharat ||
english: That great body which took form, assembled together by Saṃdhā, by which this shines today — who brought color into it?

sanskrit: sarve devā upāśikṣan tad u jānād vadhūḥ satī | īśā vaśasya yā jāyā sāsmin varṇam ābharat ||
english: All the gods sought to learn it; yet the virtuous bride knew — she who is the wife, mistress of will: she it was who brought color into it.

sanskrit: yadā tvaṣṭā vyatṛṇat pitā tvaṣṭur ya uttaraḥ | gṛhaṃ kṛtvā martyaṃ devāḥ puruṣam āviśan ||
english: When Tvaṣṭṛ had fashioned it, and the father who is beyond Tvaṣṭṛ — having made a home of the mortal, the gods entered into the person.

sanskrit: svapno vai tandrīr nirṛtiḥ pāpmāno nāma devatāḥ | jarā khālityaṃ pālityaṃ śarīram anu prāviśan ||
english: Sleep and languor, Nirṛti, and the deities named the Pāpmans — old age, baldness, and graying entered into the body.

sanskrit: steyaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vṛjinaṃ satyaṃ yajño yaśo mahaḥ | balaṃ ca kṣatram ojaś ca śarīram anu prāviśan ||
english: Theft, evil deed, and iniquity; truth, sacrifice, and great glory; strength, lordship, and vital force — all entered into the body.

sanskrit: bhūtiś ca vā abhūtiś ca rātayo 'rātayaś ca yāḥ | kṣudhaś ca sarvās tṛṣṇāś ca śarīram anu prāviśan ||
english: Prosperity and adversity, the gifts and the withheld gifts, all hungers and thirsts — all entered into the body.

sanskrit: nindyāś ca vā anindyāś ca yaś ca hanteti neti ca | śarīraṃ śraddhā dakṣiṇā- -aśraddhā cānu prāviśan ||
english: The censurable and the praiseworthy, and that which strikes and that which withholds — faith, the sacred gift, and faithlessness entered the body.

sanskrit: vidyāś ca vā avidyāś ca yac cānyad upadeśyam | śarīraṃ brahma prāviśad ṛcaḥ sāmātho yajuḥ ||
english: Knowledge and ignorance, and whatever else is teachable — Brahman entered the body: the Ṛc, the Sāman, and the Yajus.

sanskrit: ānandā nandāḥ pramudo 'bhīmodamudaś ca ye | haso nariṣṭā nṛttāni śarīram anu prāviśan ||
english: Bliss, joy, exhilaration, and the various forms of delight — laughter, festivity, and dances entered into the body.

sanskrit: ālāpāś ca pralāpāś ca- -abhīlāpalapaś ca ye | śarīraṃ sarve prāviśann āyujaḥ prayujo yujaḥ ||
english: Conversation and babble, and the various forms of excited speech and chatter — all entered the body: the unyoked, the preyoked, and the yoked.

sanskrit: prāṇāpānau cakṣuḥ śrotram akṣitiś ca kṣitiś ca yā | vyānodānau vāṅ manaḥ śarīrena ta īyante ||
english: Prāṇa and Apāna, sight and hearing, the imperishable and what perishes, Vyāna and Udāna, speech and mind — by means of the body, these move.

sanskrit: āśiṣaś ca praśiṣaś ca saṃśiṣo viśiṣaś ca yāḥ | cittāni sarve saṃkalpāḥ śarīram anu prāviśan ||
english: Blessings and commands, the shared commands and the distinct commands — all thoughts and intentions entered into the body.

sanskrit: tvarāś ca vai dhṛtayaś ca- -īḍāśīḥ sūnṛterā | śarīraṃ sarve prāviśann ṛtarīrṣyāyudho mṛdhaḥ ||
english: Urgency and steadfastness, the prayer and the auspicious word — all entered the body: those that truly strive, the weapons, the diminishers.

sanskrit: āsneyīś ca vāsteyīś ca tvaraṇāḥ kṛpaṇāś ca yāḥ | guhyāḥ śukriyā yā sthūlā bībhatsur asādhayan ||
english: The forces of blood and bone, the swift ones and the wretched — the hidden, the bright, the gross: the loathsome ones set them in order.

sanskrit: asthi kṛtvā samidhaṃ tad aṣṭāpo asādayan | retaḥ kṛtvājyaṃ devāḥ puruṣam āviśan ||
english: Making bone the sacrificial fuel, the eight waters set it in place; making semen the clarified butter, the gods entered into the person.
